title: Fill and drain with timers
summary: Run one fill, hold and drain cycle of a tank with on-delay timers, a panel start and an emergency stop.
scope: The grade runs the simulated tank in the simulator on this computer. It says nothing about a real tank, valve or sensor, its timing or its safety.
objectives: Time the steps of a process so that each timed step lasts its own time.
Use a timer as a safety limit on a step that normally ends on a sensor, and let an emergency stop abort the cycle.

stages.title: Objective
stages.body: The scene is a tank with a fill valve, a drain valve and a low-level switch, a Start button, an emergency stop and a stack light. In src/TimedTank.st, run one cycle for each press of Start while the emergency stop is released and the tank is idle: amber on, Fill open for a time set by a timer (the tank has no sensor at this level, so the timer is the measurement), a two-second hold, then Drain open until LevelLow or twenty seconds, then green on. The emergency stop closes both valves and lights red.
stages.checkpoint: The cycle is a chain of steps, and each timed step ends after its own time.

stages.title: Predict
stages.body: Before running, predict the outputs at {{t:100}} ms (before the press), at {{t:800}} ms (the cycle has started) and at {{t:1500}} ms (the emergency stop has been pressed). Then predict where the cycle stands at {{t:25000}} ms, after a second press at {{t:4000}} ms.
stages.checkpoint: {{v:TimedTank.Fill=false,TimedTank.Drain=false,TimedTank.Green=false,TimedTank.Red=false@100|Everything OFF}} at {{t:100}} ms; {{v:TimedTank.Fill=true,TimedTank.Amber=true,TimedTank.Green=false@800|Fill and Amber ON}} at {{t:800}} ms; {{v:TimedTank.Fill=false,TimedTank.Drain=false,TimedTank.Red=true@1500|both valves closed and Red ON}} at {{t:1500}} ms; {{v:TimedTank.Green=true,TimedTank.Drain=false,TimedTank.Red=false@25000|Green ON and the drain closed}} at {{t:25000}} ms.

stages.title: Edit
stages.body: Write the program, save it, then press {{ui:learn.check}}. The starter has no logic: no valve ever opens, so the cycle never runs. It declares the inputs and outputs. Each press of Start, while the emergency stop is released and the tank is idle, runs one cycle: Fill opens for 3.5 seconds, the tank holds for two seconds, then Drain opens until LevelLow or for twenty seconds at most; amber is on while the cycle runs and green once it has ended.
stages.checkpoint: The cycle runs fill, hold and drain in that order, each for its own time, and the emergency stop ends it at any point.

stages.title: Run
stages.body: Press {{ui:learn.check}}. ZPLC runs src/TimedTank.st against the tank of scene timed-tank, presses Start, operates the emergency stop and presses Start again, and tests {{assertions}} assertions: the outputs at fixed times, and that the tank never spills.
stages.checkpoint: The scenario is named timed-tank and contains {{assertions}} assertions and passes them all.

stages.title: Observe
stages.body: Watch the tank fill while Amber is on, hold, then empty until the low switch. Relate the emergency stop at {{t:1000}} ms to the step: the cycle goes back to idle, so the press at {{t:4000}} ms starts a new one.
stages.checkpoint: The trace shows a first cycle aborted at the stop and a second cycle that ends in Green.

stages.title: Reflect
stages.body: A timer measures time, not volume: if the fill valve were slower the tank would hold less after the same 3.5 seconds. The drain waits for a sensor and the timer only limits the wait.
stages.checkpoint: Name the step where a timer replaces a sensor and the step where it backs one up.

hints.text: Look at the steps of the objective one at a time: each timed step runs its own timer only while it is the active step, and the step ends when that timer is done.

Start with IF NOT EStopOk THEN Step := 0; ELSIF Step = 0 AND Start THEN Step := 1; END_IF; then one block for each step: FillT(IN := Step = 1, PT := T#3500ms) and the move to step 2 when FillT.Q is TRUE, HoldT for two seconds, DrainT for twenty seconds with the exit condition LevelLow OR DrainT.Q. Finally Fill := Step = 1; Drain := Step = 3; Amber := Step <> 0; Red := NOT EStopOk, and Green is TRUE after a finished cycle.

faultCases: The starter has no logic: no valve ever opens, so the cycle never runs.
